Timeline::hour¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::hour() const

hour() is the sole public spelling.

Read The Local Hour¶

hour() returns the hour-of-day using a 24-hour clock. Valid values are 0 through 23: midnight begins at 0, noon begins at 12, and the final hour of a day is 23. The result is shape-preserving int32; NaT becomes -1.

This is a wall-clock field, not elapsed time. Two timestamps with the same hour() may be days or years apart, and timezone conversion can change the hour while preserving the underlying instant.

Example: Midnight And Late Evening¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.hour());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[23, 0, 6, -1]

Example: Convert Before Building Local-Hour Features¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-01T00:30:00Z");
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/New_York");

std::cout << "UTC hour=" << utc.hour().item<std::int32_t>() << '\n';
std::cout << "New York hour=" << local.hour().item<std::int32_t>() << '\n';

Output¶

UTC hour=0
New York hour=19

For business-hour filters, convert to the business timezone first. Extracting in UTC and then relabeling the result cannot recover the local hour.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The clock is 24-hour; there is no AM/PM return value.

  • hour() is not a duration and cannot measure elapsed hours.

  • Repeated or skipped local hours around offset transitions are valid calendar behavior; include the date and timezone when identity matters.
